newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada unemployment edges up to 10.0 pct in October.
newsitem.headline: Canada unemployment edges up to 10.0 pct in October.

text.p: Canada's unemployment rate edged up to 10.0 percent in October from 9.9 percent in September as growth in the labour force outpaced job creation, Statistics Canada said on Friday.
The government agency said employment grew by 42,000 in October to 13.72 million. The number of people looking for work rose by 16,000 in the month, resulting in a higher unemployment rate.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast the unemployment rate to drop to 9.7 percent in October.

Despite a series of aggressive interest rate cuts by the Bank of Canada, the country's unemployment rate remained stubbornly high during the first 10 months of 1996, reflecting sluggish domestic demand in an economy relying mostly on export growth.

Statistics Canada said full-time employment rose by 44,000 from the month before, while part-time employment remained unchanged. All of the employment gains in October were in the private sector, with the self-employed accounted for two-thirds of the gains.
Employment in the construction sector rose 17,000 in October, in line with recent declines in mortgage rates and growth in housing starts.
Jobs were also created in the finance, insurance and real estate sectors, Statistics Canada said.
However, manufacturing employment fell by 30,000 in October, after growing by 108,000 in the previuos six months. The decrease follows a decline in manufacturers' shipments in August.
